inputs.original_text: Support-programme workers at the Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth are being asked to rely on government assurances while their livelihoods remain unprotected by law. Their protest outside the Presidential Palace and 24-hour strike show the imbalance of power: workers bear the risk, while the government can leave its promises unenforceable. If officials claim they have met the workers’ main demands, they should put that commitment into legally binding guarantees of job security. Rights at work should not depend on trust alone.
inputs.modified_text: Support-programme workers at the Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth are being asked to trust government promises while their jobs remain without legal protection. Their protest outside the Presidential Palace and 24-hour strike make clear who carries the risk when commitments are unenforceable: workers, not officials. If the government says it has met their main demands, it should prove it by putting job security in binding guarantees. Precarious work is a power imbalance, and workers’ rights should never rest on trust alone.
